newsitem.title: USA: El Paso Energy mulls options post-Tenneco.
newsitem.headline: El Paso Energy mulls options post-Tenneco.

text.p: As El Paso Energy Corp closes on its $4 billion acquisition of Tenneco Energy this week, Chairman William Wise said he is already mulling the company's next step in the expected consolidation of the electric and natural gas industries.

El Paso Energy was rumored to be an attractive takeover target by analysts following the announcements this year of the $7.7 billion Duke Power Co-PanEnergy Corp and $3.2 billion Enron Corp-Portland General Corp mergers.
But Wise hinted El Paso Energy may be left standing after the consolidation runs its course. "As the opportunities become available, we're going to be there," he said Tuesday.
"Whether that means we end up owning (or) being part of an electric generation company, I don't know. We're going to look at all those options," Wise said after a speech in Houston.

With the Tenneco acquisition, El Paso Energy gains control of a handful of cogeneration plants, but Wise said the company does not need to control generating capacity to be a player in the consolidated electric and gas industries.
"I don't think that's necessarily the case. What you need to have is electron liquidity and gas liquidity," he said.
